$comment: Upstream publication validators, consumed by tests/upstream.sh. Every file artefact is pinned to a full 40-hex commit SHA and verified against the recorded sha256 before it is parsed or executed, and every CLI validator is pinned to an exact version. Same rule as the `uses:` pins in .github/workflows and the CLI download in core/lib/mp-cli.sh: a mutable ref can be repointed by whoever controls the upstream repo, and this pipeline runs their code on a runner. `refName` is the human label for the pin, the counterpart of the trailing `# vX.Y.Z` on an action pin — a bare 40-hex SHA tells a reviewer nothing.
$bump: ./tests/upstream.sh --latest prints the current upstream SHAs and hashes as a ready-to-paste block. Re-run ./tests/upstream.sh afterwards: a bump that changes a validator's verdict is the signal this file exists to produce.

cursor-plugin-schema.$comment: cursor/plugins publishes no tags, so the pin is a main-branch commit. Enforced upstream by .github/workflows/validate-plugins.yml on every pull request to that repo.

codex-plugin-validator.$comment: The publication validator behind the `manifest.flavour: codex` shape documented in hosts/codex/host.json. This one is executed, not just parsed — hence the hash check is load-bearing, not decorative.

claude-code.$comment: Claude Code ships no standalone manifest schema; `claude plugin validate --strict` IS the upstream validator, so the pin is an npm version rather than a commit SHA. It checks manifest fields, skill frontmatter and component paths. It does NOT check that the plugin loads — a manifest can pass --strict and still fail at install time, which is a Tier 2 concern (install into an isolated CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR and read `claude plugin list --json` .errors), deliberately not covered here.
